source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
I see you've got copper pours on the inner layer doing the heavy lifting, but I want to confirm two things specifically for VBUS and BAT−, since those carry the worst-case current (up to ~1.5 A: 1 A charging + ~0.5 A system load simultaneously):
Are the <http://F.Cu> / <http://In2.Cu> pours contiguous all the way from the USB-C / battery connector to the AXP2101 VBUS / BAT pins, with no thin-trace bottleneck in series?
Are the stitching vias between <http://F.Cu> and <http://In2.Cu> sufficient on those nets (typically 3+ vias for ~1.5 A)?
If both are yes, I'm happy. If there's a 0.2 mm bottleneck somewhere in series, that's the part that worries me — at 1.5 A on a 0.2 mm outer trace it'd run hot (~30 °C rise above ambient).

value_updates.required_copper_path: Contiguous F.Cu/In2.Cu pours from the USB-C and battery connectors to the AXP2101 VBUS and BAT pins, without a thin-trace bottleneck in series
value_updates.stitching_via_requirement: Sufficient stitching vias between F.Cu and In2.Cu, typically 3 or more for approximately 1.5 A
